title: PsalmAnalysisOutput
description: Psalm-wide and section-wide analysis. Sections and seams come from one turn because sections must tile the psalm and agree with the seams.

summary.description: What the English setting does with the psalm as a whole, including its movement.

sections.description: The psalm's own architecture, tiled across its verses in order. first_verse/last_verse are Masoretic verse numbers.

title.description: The arrangement's name for this stretch, e.g. 'Verse 1' or 'Pre + Chorus'.

structural_seams.description: Structural articulations in the received text, such as Selah. An empty array when the psalm has none.

aligns_with_section.description: Whether an arrangement section ends here. A structural-fidelity signal, not a value judgement.

guardrails.description: Both answers are required every time, so neither can be quietly skipped.

epistemics.description: The boundary of what the text supports. Each claim carries its grounds so a reviewer can check it rather than take it on trust.

basis.description: The words or feature of the text this rests on.

non_source_material.description: Arrangement apparatus that applies to the whole setting rather than one verse.

method.description: How the literal renderings were arrived at and against what they were checked.

citations.description: Lexica, editions and discussions relied on. Free-form strings; an empty array is honest when nothing beyond the supplied evidence was used.

similar_translations.description: Existing translations the English resembles, closest first. Wording every translation shares is no resemblance; an empty array is honest when none stands out.

translation.description: The translation by name, e.g. 'King James Version' or 'Scottish Metrical Psalter (1650)'.

basis.description: supplied: compared with text given in the prompt. recalled: recognised from the auditor's own knowledge of a published translation, which the reviewer cannot check here.

closeness.description: reproduces: its wording throughout, small changes aside. adapts: follows it closely, reworded or re-metered. echoes: shares distinctive phrasing in places.

evidence.description: Which verses, and the wording they share. Quote a recalled translation by a few words at most.
